SA NB 1. Consenting to Assignment of Certain Contractual Rights and Obligations by Clutter Motors, Inc. to Sully III AVP, LLC
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. SA 03-17, consenting to assignment of certain contractual rights and obligations by Clutter Motors, Inc. to Sully III AVP, LLC and approving and authorizing execution of documents related thereto.
SA NB 1
SA NB 1 attachment
Clutter Motors, Inc. ("Clutter") and the Former Redevelopment Agency previously entered into various agreements (collectively, the "Dealership Agreements") concerning Clutter's operation of one or more automobile dealerships in the City. Clutter has requested that the Successor Agency consent to its assignment of certain rights and obligations created by the Dealership Agreements to Sully III AVP, LLC ("Sully"), as further described in the Assignment and Assumption Agreement (the "Assignment and Assumption Agreement"). Additionally, Sully has requested that the Successor Agency agree to subordinate the deed of trust that secures performance under the Dealership Agreements in order to facilitate certain financing Sully seeks to obtain, as further described in the Subordination Agreement (the "Subordination Agreement").

CC 4. Adopt Ordinance No. 1019, (the "Ordinance"), adding Chapters 5.56 and 17.43 to the Lancaster Municipal Code relating to the regulation of medical cannabis; with specific prohibitions banning dispensaries, outdoor cultivation, distribution facilities, and delivery businesses in the City of Lancaster; and imposing stringent regulations upon indoor cultivation/manufacturing in limited zones.
The Ordinance includes specific prohibitions such as banning dispensaries, outdoor cultivation, distribution facilities, and delivery businesses in the City of Lancaster. The Ordinance would establish a comprehensive regulatory scheme requiring cultivators to apply for and obtain both (i) a City-issued cultivator's license and (ii) a conditional use permit. Under the Ordinance, a Cultivator's license would be subject to various requirements and limitations related to security and operation. Under the Ordinance, a conditional use permit for the cultivation of cannabis would similarly be subject to various requirements and limitations. The Ordinance conditionally permits only medical cannabis cultivation/manufacturing facilities and allows the City Council to limit the number of such facilities by resolution.

The rehabilitation work being performed by the contractor will consist of the following: eliminating safety concerns, including fire hazards, lead-based paint hazards, removing unpermitted construction and correcting code violations; installing more energy efficient systems, including water conservation devices, and making general property and green building improvements that will increase the long-term sustainability of the single family residence

Retention on this project has been disbursed in accordance with California Public Contract Code.
On January 26, 2016, Council awarded Public Works Construction Project No. 14-008, Avenue K-8 Bike Path Improvements, BTA 12/13-07-LA-06 to Granite Construction Company. Bike path improvements from Sierra Highway to 15th Street West along Avenue K-8, as well as a new signalized pedestrian crossing at Sierra Highway and Avenue K-8, and signal improvements at Avenue K-8 and 10th Street West were constructed. Construction of the project has been completed to the satisfaction of the Development Services Director. The project was completed on January 30, 2017, which was within the time permitted in the contract.
PUBLIC HEARING

CC 7 attachment
PH 1. Appeals of Planning Commission Decisions approving the following requests:
* Conditional Use Permit No.'s 16-02a and 16-02b, requests to construct a 50-megawatt photovoltaic solar generating facility on 307 acres in the RR-2.5 zone, generally bounded by Avenue F, 95th Street West, Avenue G, and 100th Street West; and
* Conditional Use Permit No.'s 16-07a and 16-07b, requests to construct a 15-megawatt photovoltaic solar generating facility on 177 acres in the RR-2.5 zone, generally bounded by Avenue F, 100th Street West, Avenue F-8, and 105th Street West.
Recommendations:
PH 1
PH 1 attachment
a.
Adopt Resolution No. 17-08, upholding the Planning Commission decision and approving Conditional Use Permit No. 16-02a and Conditional Use Permit No. 16-02b.
b.
Adopt Resolution No. 17-09, upholding the Planning Commission decision and approving Conditional Use Permit No. 16-07a and Conditional Use Permit No. 16-07b.
The Planning Commission held an initial hearing on the requested conditional use permits at their regular meeting of December 19, 2016. The Commission received a number of written and oral comments at this meeting, and continued the matter to their regular meeting of January 17, 2017, in order to allow sufficient time for review and response to the issues raised. During that meeting, the Commission heard additional testimony regarding the proposed projects, and considered the issues in light of the evidence presented. Following the hearing, the Planning Commission voted (by a 6-1 vote) to approve the conditional use permits. The Planning Commission, in its review and consideration of the testimony provided, considered the issues raised by the appellant, specifically 1) Dust; 2) Zoning, Setback and Landscaping; 3) Traffic and Roadways; 4) Cumulative Impacts; and 5) Aesthetics. Staff believes that the proposed projects are consistent with the City's zoning requirements for the site, and that the conditions of approval proposed for the projects will adequately mitigate both potential impacts during the construction phase, as well as during long-term operation of the projects.
NEW BUSINESS
NB 1. Approval of Amendment to Disposition and Development Agreement with BYD
Recommendation:
Approve the Second Amendment to the Disposition and Development Agreement with BYD Approve the Second Amendment to the Disposition and Development Agreement with BYD Energy, LLC and BYD Coach & Bus, LLC (collectively referred to as BYD), thus authorizing a shift in the City's previously agreed-upon incentive responsibility to providing off-site public improvements required in association with BYD's expansion; and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute all related documents.
NB 1
NB 1 attachment
This amendment will allow the City of Lancaster to satisfy its commitment to BYD while facilitating the expansion of a world-class company that, just three years after breaking into the U.S. market, has already emerged as the top competitor in the manufacture of electric buses nationwide. BYD's current expansion plans will create hundreds of additional jobs for Lancaster residents in the near term, with untold opportunities for further growth well into the future.
NB 2. Ordinance Prohibiting Nonmedical Marijuana Businesses
Recommendations:
NB 2
NB 2 attachment
a.
Introduce Ordinance No. 1021, (the â€œOrdinanceâ€), adding Chapter 5.60 to the Lancaster Municipal Code relating to the prohibition of nonmedical marijuana businesses.
b.
Provide direction to staff regarding further restrictions on nonmedical marijuana within the City as allowed by law.
This Ordinance prohibits to the fullest extent allowed by law nonmedical commercial recreational marijuana activities of all types including, but not limited to, the sale, transportation, distribution, cultivation, possession, manufacturing, delivery, testing, storing, labeling, and processing and personal cultivation of marijuana outdoors. This Ordinance also authorizes the City Manager to promulgate such regulations as may be necessary or convenient to implement the Ordinance, including, without limitation, reasonable regulations for the cultivation of nonmedical marijuana that occurs inside a residence or accessory structure. Any violation of this Ordinance is a misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine in an amount to be established by resolution of the City Council, or by imprisonment for a period of not more than six (6) months, or by both.
